newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU resumes offensive on BA/American pact.
newsitem.headline: EU resumes offensive on BA/American pact.

text.p: The European Commission, hinting that the British election truce has lasted long enough, has relaunched its offensive on the proposed alliance between British Airways BA and AMR's American Airlines.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert met British Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett on Tuesday in London to say what he has already made crystal clear -- that the deal will not get the EU's blessing as it stands.

The two sides declined to comment as is usual in large, market-sensitive alliances as this one, but EU sources had expected Van Miert to tell the new British government that the proposed alliance would harm competition particularly between the United States and Britain.
The Commission may make an official statement towards the end of the week, a Commission source said, although it was unclear what its purpose might be.
It refrained from making any statements during the election campaign, but has now decided to forge ahead with its conclusions.

Van Miert said in a letter to Beckett's predecessor Ian Lang in January that the deal would eliminate competition on 13 routes between the U.S. and Britain and warned he would take legal action if the British authorities ignored the Commission's concerns.

The companies themselves were informed of the Commission's grievances in a so-called statement of objections at the end of last year. But British Airways said on Tuesday the Commission had not discussed its concerns with the company.

"In the Commission's own words, (the analysis of the deal) will take some time to complete. It would be very natural for the Commission to discuss their concerns with us before reaching a conclusion and this they have not done," a spokesman said,
The content of any new Commission statement, and indeed the decision to issue one, depended very much on what Britain's new Labour government told Van Miert, the sources said.
Labour expressed doubts about the deal during the election campaign, but nuanced its position before it won the general elections on May 1 by an overwhelmingly majority.

The Department of Trade and Industry is still expecting the country's Office of Fair Trading to give its final ruling. In December, the OFT proposed clearing the alliance on the condition that the two airlines gave up 168 weekly landing and take-off slots at the congested London Heathrow airport.
But Van Miert made clear in the January letter that this would not be enough.

The new statement, which would be the first since the Commission opened its probe into BA-American and a string of other transatlantic deals in July 1996, could outline the Commission's doubts, one source said.
The statement would put the ball in the Britain's and the companies' camp. "We cannot say that this is the end. Whatever the parties say, they must move now," the source said.
The former British government argued that it, not the Commission, had authority over the deal, which would create the world's largest aviation grouping.

The Commission has repeatedly asserted that it must vet the alliance under EU competition rules because it would affect air transport services not only between Britain and the U.S. but also with the rest of the EU's territory.

Under article 89 of the treaty of Rome, it must work in cooperation with the British authorities when investigating the case but if needed "it shall propose appropriate measures" to ensure fair competition.

The Commission made a fresh bid on Tuesday to revise 1987 EU legislation on the application of competition rules to air transport services to give it clearer powers over air pacts between EU and non-EU carriers.
Although Van Miert's spokesman insisted this was not linked with the review of the BA-American alliance, it is clearly an attempt to avoid legal battles in the future.
British Airways shares fell 10-1/2 pence to 725-1/2 on the news that the Commission was still seeking changes in the deal and had lost further ground to 718-1/2 at 1415GMT.
